Road joined to the valley entrance

Welcome to the valley, governor. Settlers will come from the west, through the pass in the forest, but only along a road. Lay a road from the valley entrance into the open land: click Road, then drag.

Q and E turn the view, the mouse wheel zooms, WASD moves.

Mark out house lots beside the road. Settlers will build Thatched Huts on them. Every home needs water: a Well serves the houses around it.

Space pauses the game; 1, 2 and 3 set the speed.

People eat every day. Rice Paddies grow rice on the fertile plain by the river, carriers take it to a Granary, and a Market buys it there. Its vendor walks the streets near the Market and fills the pantries.

Click any building to see what it is doing and what it lacks. F2 shows which houses have food.

A Village Shrine keeps the neighborhood's spirits at peace. Its keeper walks the streets near it, and houses visited by the keeper grow into Thatched Houses.

Guardian Posts stand on a road and mark where a walker's round ends: use them to keep vendors and keepers on the streets that need them.

Thatched Houses want Clay Jars to keep their food. Dig clay with a Clay Pit on a rocky hill, cut wood with a Woodcutter by the forest, and fire both in a Pottery Kiln. A Storehouse keeps clay, wood and jars; the Market sells the jars.

F4 opens the Goods window: what the city has, and where it is short.

Soybean Paste is the soul of the kitchen. Soybean Fields and Salt Pans on the shore send soybeans and salt to a Fermentation Yard, where the paste rests in clay jars. Fresh paste is ready in ten days; Ripe paste lasts twice as long but needs two more seasons.

Keep the yard close to the fields and the salt: every load is carried on someone's back.

A Tiled House needs good Gi, the life force of the land. Gi is high below the mountain, near water and between the forest ridges; Clay Pits, Kilns and Woodcutters lower it, Village Shrines and Guardian Posts raise it.

Press F7 to see the Gi of the valley. Gold marks the Myeongdang, the best places of all.

The hill folk talk of dokkaebi: mischievous goblins who come at night to storages where the Gi is low. Watch for their blue fires in the hills: they come five days later.

Guardian Posts on the road turn them back. An offering of buckwheat jelly at a Village Shrine appeases them, and pleased dokkaebi sometimes leave Silver.

You know everything Seorabeol needs. Now let it grow: 300 people and ten Tiled Houses, with rice, paste and jars reaching every street.

When something is short, the Goods window and the building windows say where and why.
Move the view to the advisor's arrow: a good spot for the next building.
